stem: What is the module format for a stick of SODIMM DDR4 RAM?
explanation: DDR4 SODIMM modules have 260 pins. DDR5 SODIMMs use 262 pins, so the two cannot be swapped in the same slot.
whyWrong: 1.8-inch is a size for small laptop storage drives, not a memory module format.
262 pins is the DDR5 SODIMM format, not DDR4.
2.5-inch is the standard size for laptop SSD and HDD storage drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: You just added a second memory module to a laptop. However, after you reboot the system, the OS reports the same amount of memory as before. What should you do NEXT?
explanation: The next step you should take is to reseat the memory. SODIMMs can be a bit tricky to install. They must be firmly installed, but you don’t want to press too hard and damage any components.
whyWrong: If the laptop worked fine before the upgrade, there is no reason to replace both modules yet.
Windows Update does not find or enable additional RAM.
Replacing the motherboard is a last resort and is not justified when the laptop worked before the upgrade.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which of the following are ways that a laptop can communicate with other computers? (Select all that apply.)
explanation: Some of the methods that laptops use to communicate with other computers include Bluetooth, WLAN, and cellular WAN wireless connections, plus wired connections like Ethernet (RJ-45) and, for older laptops, dial-up (RJ-11). Each wireless method relies on its own radio card or module inside the laptop.
whyWrong: The DC jack is the input on the laptop that accepts power from the AC adapter, not a communication port.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Which of the following are possible reasons that a laptop’s keyboard might fail completely? (Select the two best answers.)
options: The user spilled coffee on the laptop.
The keyboard was disabled in the Device Manager.
explanation: A laptop’s keyboard could fail due to a disconnected or loose keyboard ribbon cable. It could also fail if a user spilled coffee on the laptop, dropped it on the ground, and so on.
whyWrong: One stuck key will not cause the entire keyboard to fail.
On most laptops the keyboard can be uninstalled in Device Manager but not disabled.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: A user doesn’t see anything on his laptop’s screen. He tries to use AC power and thinks that the laptop is not receiving any. Which of the following are two possible reasons for this? (Select the two best answers.)
options: He is using an incorrect AC adapter.
The AC adapter is not connected to the laptop.
explanation: An incorrect adapter will usually not power a laptop. The adapter used must be exact. And, of course, if the laptop is not properly plugged into the adapter, it won’t get power.
whyWrong: Windows does not affect whether the laptop receives AC power.
A dead battery matters only when the AC adapter is also disconnected, and the user is trying to run on AC power.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: One of your customers reports that she walked away from her laptop for 30 minutes, and when she returned, the display was very dim. She increased the brightness setting and moved the mouse but to no effect. What should you do FIRST?
options: Check the operating system for corruption.
Connect an external monitor to verify that the video card works.
Check whether the laptop is now on battery power.
explanation: It could be that the laptop is now on battery power and is set to a dimmer display and shorter sleep configuration while on battery. The laptop may not be getting AC power from the AC outlet for some reason. The battery power setting is the first thing you should check; afterward, start troubleshooting the AC adapter, cable, AC outlet, and so on.
whyWrong: It is too early to replace the display before you rule out simpler causes such as the power source.
A dim screen is not caused by OS corruption.
The video adapter is clearly working because the screen shows an image, only a dim one.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware, Cram Quiz question 6
note: Laptop power troubleshooting; the current book teaches it under 1.1 (Power). Could also fit 220-1201/5.4.

stem: You are helping a customer with a laptop issue. The customer says that two days ago the laptop was accidentally dropped while it was charging. You observe that the laptop will not turn on and that it is connected to the correct power adapter. Which of the following is the MOST LIKELY cause?
explanation: The DC jack was probably damaged when the laptop was dropped. It may have been plugged in (charging) and fallen on the plug that connects to the DC jack (which is easily damaged on many laptops). The customer probably used the laptop until the battery became discharged before noticing that the laptop wouldn’t take a charge anymore—and now it won’t turn on at all.
whyWrong: The battery most likely just ran down because the damaged DC jack stopped it from charging.
A power adapter can be damaged, but the DC-in jack is more easily damaged in a fall.
The storage drive normally does not affect whether the laptop turns on.
The BIOS/UEFI normally does not affect whether the laptop powers on.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware, Cram Quiz question 7
note: Laptop power hardware; the current book teaches it under 1.1 (Power). Could also fit 220-1201/5.4 (physically damaged ports).

stem: You want to reduce the risk of your laptop being stolen. Which of the following is the BEST option?
explanation: To best reduce the chance of theft, use a cable lock. This physical cable can be wrapped around a sturdy object and locked to the laptop, keeping it relatively secure from theft. The other choices can decrease the chance of data being stolen, but none of them reduce the risk of the laptop itself being stolen.
whyWrong: Biometrics adds a fingerprint or other physical scan to sign-in, which protects data but does not stop the laptop from being carried away.
Disabling NFC stops data from being beamed to other devices but does nothing against physical theft.
MFA combines factors such as a password and biometrics to protect sign-in, not the hardware.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware, Cram Quiz question 8

stem: A user cannot make contactless payments using NFC, connect to the Internet, or send/receive calls from a mobile device. The user is able to boot the device and sign on. Which of the following is MOST LIKELY the cause of the problem?
explanation: Turning on airplane mode (the most likely cause of the problem) will disable wireless transmissions, including NFC. This is great for security purposes, but it can also disable the ability to connect to Wi-Fi networks or send/receive calls.
whyWrong: A failed power state would make the whole device unusable, but the user can boot and sign on.
Biometric authentication is not the cause because the user has no trouble signing on.
ESD can damage components, but the device works normally in every other way.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware, Cram Quiz question 9

stem: Which of the following allows you to access a WLAN?
explanation: A Wi-Fi card, also known as a Wi-Fi network adapter, allows you to connect to a wireless local area network (WLAN), which is essentially another name for a Wi-Fi network. In laptops it is usually a small internal card, often an M.2 2230 module, wired to antennas in the display.
whyWrong: LED is a type of display, not a network adapter.
A webcam is used to communicate visually and audibly with others or to record oneself.
A digitizer converts tapped or written impulses on a screen into digital information for the operating system.
A stylus is a writing device used with a digitizer or touchscreen.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware, Cram Quiz question 10

stem: You have been tasked with replacing a Wi-Fi/Bluetooth card in a laptop. You open the laptop and find a card that uses the 2230 standard. What type of card is this?
explanation: The 2230 standard is a kind of M.2 size measuring 22×30 mm. It is common in laptops for use with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. In comparison, a PC often uses a 2280 M.2 card.
whyWrong: Mini PCI is an older card slot that does not use size codes such as 2230 or 2280.
A digitizer is not a card or port but a device that converts tapped impulses into digital information.
RJ-45 is a wired networking port, not an internal card.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware, Cram Quiz question 11

stem: What would you MOST LIKELY need to do to replace a Wi-Fi card antenna cable in a laptop?
options: Remove the current module by pushing both of the clips out.
Insert the new module at a 45-degree angle into slot.
Press down again to make sure the module is in place.
Open the display to replace the cable.
explanation: Most often in laptops, the antenna is located in the display area of the laptop. You will most likely need to separate the display from the laptop’s motherboard section to open it and replace the antenna cable.
whyWrong: Pushing both clips out is how you remove a SODIMM memory module, not an antenna cable.
Inserting a module at a 45-degree angle is a step for installing a SODIMM.
Pressing down to seat the module is the last step of a SODIMM installation.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware, Cram Quiz question 12

stem: Which of the following are storage drive form factors for laptops? (Choose three.)
explanation: Laptop storage drive types include SSD, magnetic disk, and hybrid. Also, be aware that they have either 2.5- or 1.8-inch form factors. In addition, M.2 form factor storage drives have become more popular in modern laptops.
whyWrong: SODIMM is the form factor of laptop RAM, not of a storage drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware, Cram Quiz question 13

stem: You are required to add long-term storage to a smartphone. Which type would you MOST LIKELY add?
explanation: You would most likely add a microSD card (if the smartphone has a slot available for add-ons or upgrading). This is the most common method for adding long-term storage.
whyWrong: DDR4 is a type of RAM and is not used to add long-term storage.
LPDDR4 is smartphone main memory built into the system on a chip, not user-added storage.
An SSD is a SATA or M.2 drive for PCs and laptops and is too large for a smartphone.
A SIM card stores subscriber authentication data such as the IMSI, not user files.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options, Cram Quiz question 2
note: Exam Cram Chapter 2 (1.2); mobile device storage is tagged with the closest current topic, 1.1 HDD/SSD.

stem: A laptop’s battery fails to charge. Which of the following should be checked FIRST?
explanation: Of the listed answers, you should check the DC-in jack on the laptop first. However, the very first thing you should do is check the basics: See if the power brick is connected to the AC outlet and to the DC-in jack and verify that the battery is connected properly. A damaged DC-in jack is common because users often leave the power adapter plugged in while they are in transit.
whyWrong: Laptops have no AC-in jack, because the power adapter converts AC power to DC for the laptop.
The CMOS battery retains UEFI/BIOS settings and has nothing to do with charging the main laptop battery.
A tripped AC circuit breaker is less likely, and it would also stop every other device on that circuit.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 7
note: Laptop power hardware; the current book teaches it under 1.1 (Power). Could also fit 220-1201/5.4 (improper charging).

stem: You replaced a bad internal WLAN card in a Windows laptop. You completed the installation and verified that the new WLAN card is listed in the Device Manager as enabled. What should you do NEXT to actually use the card?
options: Update the firmware of the WLAN card.
Add the SSID of the network to the connection.
explanation: Next, connect to a wireless network: scan for the network names (SSIDs) or add the SSID of the network manually. After you select the network, you enter its security passphrase.
whyWrong: You type the security passphrase only after you select a wireless network to connect to.
Firmware and driver updates for the card belong to the installation, which is already complete.
If the router accepts wireless connections, its encryption is already configured.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 46

stem: A client has a laptop with which you are unfamiliar. You are asked to perform a memory upgrade. How can you obtain the service manual for this laptop computer?
options: By pressing F1 while in Windows
By pressing F2 while the system is booting up
By reading the paper copy that comes with the laptop
explanation: Laptop service manuals can be obtained from the manufacturer's website. It's very rare that paper service manuals are shipped with the laptop. The service manual shows how to reach the memory slots and which modules the laptop supports.
whyWrong: Pressing F1 while in Windows opens Windows Help, not the laptop's service manual.
Pressing F2 during boot on many laptops opens the BIOS/UEFI setup, not a service manual.
Paper service manuals are very rarely shipped with a laptop.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 1

stem: You need to replace defective DDR4 memory in a laptop. How many pins will the replacement memory module have?
explanation: DDR4 SODIMMs have 260 pins. DDR2 SODIMMs have 200 pins, DDR3 SODIMMs have 204 pins, and DDR5 SODIMMs have 262. No SODIMMs currently have 288 pins, but DDR4 DIMMs do.
whyWrong: A 200-pin module is a DDR2 SODIMM.
A 204-pin module is a DDR3 SODIMM.
288 pins is the count of a desktop DDR4 DIMM, not a laptop SODIMM.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 6

stem: A user is getting a new laptop. Which of the following is not a valid option to get his files and data from the old hard drive to the new hard drive?
options: Manually copy files from the old drive to the cloud, and then to the new drive.
Manually copy files from the old drive to an external hard drive, and then to the new drive.
Use a hard drive migration app.
Use the NFC disk transfer utility.
explanation: To migrate data from one hard drive to another, you can manually copy the data or use a migration app. There is no NFC disk transfer utility.
whyWrong: Copying files to cloud storage and then down to the new drive is a valid manual migration method.
Copying files to an external hard drive and then to the new drive is a valid manual migration method.
A hard drive migration app is a valid way to move files and data to a new drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 11
note: The book's 220-1201 chapter keeps the HDD/SSD migration content; current 1.1 lists HDD/SSD without a migration sub-bullet.

stem: A user has requested a laptop memory upgrade. The technician attempts to put in new memory, but the memory module is barely too wide for the slot. What is the MOST LIKELY scenario?
options: The technician is trying to install DDR4 into a motherboard with DDR3 slots.
The technician is trying to install DDR3 into a motherboard with DDR4 slots.
The technician is trying to install MicroDIMMs into SODIMM slots.
The technician is trying to install DIMMs into SODIMM slots.
explanation: Laptops most often use SODIMMs (or possibly MicroDIMMs), which are much smaller than standard DIMMs used in desktops. DDR2 and DDR3 SODIMMs are 67.6 millimeters wide, whereas DDR4 SODIMMs are 69.6 millimeters wide. It's likely that the technician has DDR4 SODIMMs and the motherboard supports DDR3 SODIMMs.
whyWrong: A DDR3 SODIMM is narrower than a DDR4 slot, so it would not be too wide for it.
MicroDIMMs are smaller than SODIMMs, so they would not be too wide for a SODIMM slot.
Desktop DIMMs are much larger than SODIMMs, not barely too wide.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 13

stem: The process by which the processor slows down to conserve power is officially called ____________.
explanation: The processor can reduce how fast it's working, which is called throttling, to help conserve battery life. Most laptops run the processor in a lower power state on battery power and throttle it back up when more processing power is needed.
whyWrong: Underclocking is a manual setting to run a component below its rated speed, not the automatic power-saving process.
Cooling removes heat from the processor; it is not the process of slowing it down.
Disengaging is not a CPU power management process.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 15
note: Processor throttling to save battery is power management; tagged to Battery (1.1), the closest current topic.

stem: You need to replace a failed AC adapter for a client's laptop. When replacing the adapter, which of the following purchases is acceptable to obtain the same or better results?
options: An AC adapter with a higher voltage rating than the original
An AC adapter with a higher wattage rating than the original
A DC adapter with the same voltage rating as the original
An AC adapter with a lower voltage and wattage rating than the original
explanation: Think of wattage as a “bucket” of power that the attached device can draw from. A bigger bucket simply holds more power but does not force the power on the device. Voltage can be thought of as the pressure behind the power to the device, and anything but the proper voltage is dangerous for the device. When you replace a laptop's AC adapter, you should match the voltage ratings of the original adapter.
whyWrong: A higher voltage than the original can damage the laptop; the voltage must match.
A laptop needs an AC adapter that plugs into wall power, not a DC adapter.
A lower voltage and wattage cannot properly power the laptop.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 16
note: Laptop power adapter replacement; tagged to Battery (1.1), the closest current topic.

stem: What should you do for a Li-ion battery that appears to charge fully but does not last as long as the battery's meter indicates that it will last?
options: Short the terminals to discharge the battery.
explanation: Battery calibration for Li-ion batteries allows the powered device to drain the battery's power before recharging. This resets the battery meter so that it reports the remaining charge correctly. Replacement is a last resort, used when a battery has reached the end of its life.
whyWrong: Replacement is a last resort for a battery at the end of its life, not the first fix for a wrong meter.
Battery exercising is the initial charging and discharging of nickel-based batteries, not Li-ion.
You should never short a battery's terminals.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 17

stem: You are giving a seminar to new technicians on replacing laptop hard drives. A student asks how do laptop hard drives differ from desktop hard drives. What do you tell them?
options: Laptop hard drives use completely different standards from those used by desktop hard drives for communication with the host.
Laptop hard drives are solid-state, whereas desktop hard drives have spinning platters.
Laptop hard drives require a separate power connection, whereas desktop hard drives are powered through the drive interface.
The most common form factors for laptop hard drives is smaller than that of a desktop hard drive.
explanation: Laptop hard drives commonly have a 2½″ form factor, and smaller drives, such as M.2, are becoming more popular. The most common form factor for desktop hard drives is 3½″. Laptop hard drives use the same drive technologies as their desktop counterparts, such as SATA.
whyWrong: Laptop drives use the same standards as desktop drives, such as SATA.
Laptop and desktop drives are both available as solid-state and spinning-platter drives.
Laptop hard drives do not have separate power connectors; desktop drives do.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 18

stem: Which multimedia device is used for Internet video communication, which allows people to interact over networks with both voice and video?
explanation: A webcam allows people to interact over networks with both voice and video. Most webcams also include a built-in microphone.
whyWrong: A speaker plays sound but does not capture video.
A microphone captures voice but not video.
A sound processor handles audio inside the computer and does not capture video.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 10: Essential Peripherals, Chapter Review question 8
note: Older book (220-1101/1102), All-in-One 11e Chapter 10: multimedia peripherals. Closest current topic: 220-1201/1.1 Camera/webcam.

stem: Which of the following are good ideas when it comes to batteries? (Select two.)
options: Keep the contacts clean by using alcohol and a soft cloth.
Store them in the freezer if they will not be used for a long period of time.
Toss them in the garbage when they wear out.
Store them in a cool, dry place.
explanation: Clean battery contacts with a little alcohol on a soft cloth, and store a battery you will not use for a while in a cool, dry place. Keeping a battery in the freezer is a good idea in theory, but not in practice. All batteries contain toxic chemicals and should never be treated like regular trash.
whyWrong: Cold storage in a freezer risks condensation and damage, so it is not a good practice for batteries.
Batteries contain toxic chemicals and must be recycled, not thrown in the garbage.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 23: Portable Computing, Chapter Review question 1

stem: To replace a wireless antenna in a laptop, what must you do?
options: Remove the expansion slot cover on the bottom of the laptop.
explanation: The antenna for laptop Wi-Fi connections is located in the screen portion of the laptop. To access the antenna, remove the screen (or at least the plastic frame parts).
whyWrong: The antenna wires run up into the display, so removing the keyboard does not reach the antenna.
The bottom panel gives access to the wireless card, but the antenna itself sits in the display.
A laptop Wi-Fi antenna can be replaced once the screen or its bezel is taken apart.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 23: Portable Computing, Chapter Review question 2

stem: Which of the following SSD form factors are commonly used in laptops? (Select two.)
explanation: 2.5-inch and M.2 solid-state drives are commonly used in laptops. M.2 cards are small and plug straight into a slot on the motherboard, while 2.5-inch drives use the same bay as a laptop hard drive.
whyWrong: 3.5-inch drives are desktop drives and are too large for a laptop.
1.8-inch drives were used in a few older ultraportables but are not common today.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 23: Portable Computing, Chapter Review question 3

stem: Steve complains that his aging Windows laptop still isn’t snappy enough after upgrading the RAM. What might improve system performance?
options: Replace the HDD with an SSD.
explanation: Replacing the HDD with an SSD will speed up the system. An SSD has no moving parts, so it boots, loads programs, and reads files much faster than a spinning hard drive.
whyWrong: Steve already upgraded the RAM, so the slow hard drive is the likely bottleneck.
The power supply does not limit how fast the system runs.
A new battery gives longer run time, not better performance.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 23: Portable Computing, Chapter Review question 7

stem: Jim likes his laptop but complains that his wireless seems slow compared to all the new laptops. On further inspection, you determine his laptop runs 802.11n. What can be done to improve his network connection speed?
options: Replace the display with one with a better antenna.
Replace the 802.11n card with an 802.11ac card.
Get a new laptop, because this one can’t be upgraded.
explanation: Replacing the 802.11n wireless card with an 802.11ac NIC should improve his network connection speed. Laptop wireless cards are usually M.2 or Mini PCIe modules that a technician can swap after removing a service panel.
whyWrong: More RAM does not change the speed of the wireless link.
The antenna is not what limits the speed; the 802.11n standard of the card is.
Most laptops let you replace the wireless card, so a new laptop is not required.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 23: Portable Computing, Chapter Review question 8

stem: Edgar successfully replaced the display on a laptop (a toddler had taken a ballpoint pen to it), but the customer called back almost immediately complaining that his wireless didn’t work. What could the problem be?
options: The problems are unrelated, so it could be anything.
Edgar inadvertently disconnected the antenna from the 802.11 card.
Edgar replaced the display with one without an internal antenna.
Edgar failed to reconnect the antenna in the new display.
explanation: The Wi-Fi antenna wires run through the laptop display, so a display replacement means disconnecting and reconnecting them. A disconnected antenna makes Wi-Fi unhappy, so Edgar most likely failed to reconnect the antenna in the new display.
whyWrong: The problems are related, because the antenna wires sit in the display Edgar just replaced.
The antenna leads attach to the 802.11 card, but the likely fault is in the new display he connected, not the card side.
Replacement laptop displays include the antenna, so a display without one is unlikely.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 23: Portable Computing, Chapter Review question 9

stem: Which of the following is the most secure method to set up a laptop or desktop to use biometric readers?
options: Set up the laptop/desktop for the person who uses the device
Set up the laptop/desktop so everyone in the accounts department can log in
Allow other departments access to the laptop/desktop
Set up the laptop for user access and allow guest access
explanation: The biometric reader should be set up on each laptop or desktop for only the user of that device. In the accounts department, only one person should have access to each device.
whyWrong: Some users in accounts handle more sensitive data than others, so letting the whole department log in to one device is not secure.
Employees from other departments should not be able to log in to an accounts department device.
Guest access gives people from outside the company a way into company resources.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.1 question 1
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.1 (laptop hardware); biometrics is a physical security component in current 1.1.

stem: A hardware engineer is going to upgrade the RAM in a laptop. Before installing the new RAM, which of the following tasks should the hardware engineer complete FIRST?
options: Take anti-static precautions by wearing an electrostatic discharge strap
Check the power voltage to the motherboard
Download any operating system updates for the laptop’s operating system
explanation: Before handling RAM, wear an electrostatic discharge (ESD) strap to protect the module from static electricity. Memory modules are easily damaged by static discharge from the body.
whyWrong: Laptops use SODIMM modules, and no 256 GB DDR3 module exists.
Checking the power voltage to the motherboard is a step for power problems, not a RAM upgrade.
Operating system updates have no relationship to a RAM upgrade.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.1 question 2
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.1 (laptop hardware)

stem: What type of RAM would you purchase for a laptop computer?
explanation: A Small Outline Dual In-Line Memory Module (SODIMM) is smaller and thinner so that it fits into a laptop that has restricted space. Laptops use SODIMMs, while desktops use full-size DIMMs.
whyWrong: A Dual In-Line Memory Module (DIMM) is about twice the length of a SODIMM and is used in desktops, workstations, and servers.
DDR3 is a memory generation, not a laptop form factor; it comes in both DIMM and SODIMM versions.
SDRAM describes the memory technology, and its full-size modules are used in desktop computers.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.1 question 4
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.1 (laptop hardware)

stem: Which of the following safety precautions do you need to take prior to installing an SSD into a user’s laptop? ( Choose four)
options: Ground yourself by wearing an ESD strap
explanation: When installing a Solid-State Drive (SSD) into a laptop, you must first shut the system down, then disconnect the power cable and remove the battery. You must then ground yourself by wearing an Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) wrist strap to protect the components against the static electricity in your body.
whyWrong: Clearing your desk is good practice, but it is not a safety precaution.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.1 question 5
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.1 (laptop hardware)

stem: Which of the following stages do you need to take when migrating a Hard Drive (HDD) to a Solid-State Drive (SSD) in a laptop? (Select all that apply)
options: Clean the files on your old hard drive and remove redundant data
Make a full backup of your system
Resize the old HDD partition where your data resides to be smaller than the SSD
Restore the data onto the SSD
explanation: All of the listed stages are part of migrating a laptop from an HDD to an SSD. First make a full backup of the HDD in case anything goes wrong, then remove redundant data and resize the data partition so it is smaller than the SSD. Next clone the old HDD partition, install and initialize the SSD, and finally restore the cloned data onto the SSD.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.1 question 9
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.1 (laptop hardware). Every option is correct (book 'Select all that apply').

stem: A new door access system uses a 13.56-MHz short-band frequency. Which of the following can be used for authentication with this system on a mobile device?
explanation: A 13.56-MHz frequency is used by RFID applications, including Near-Field Communication (NFC). NFC is the scanner type used in door access and card payment systems, and a phone with NFC can act as the access card.
whyWrong: Biometrics authenticates with a fingerprint or face, not with a 13.56-MHz radio signal from the phone.
Certificates prove identity for encryption and digital signatures, not over a short-range door reader.
Open Authorization (OAuth) is an internet-based authorization framework, not a radio access method.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.1 question 10
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.1 (laptop hardware); NFC door access is a near-field scanner feature in current 1.1.

stem: A computer technician is going to install a Solid-State Drive (SSD) in a laptop. What is the standard form factor of the drive that the computer technician needs to purchase?
explanation: Most Solid-State Drives (SSDs) for laptops come in a 2.5-inch standard form factor. Many newer laptops use M.2 SSDs instead, but 2.5 inches is the standard drive size for a laptop drive bay.
whyWrong: 3.5 inches is the size of a desktop hard drive; a 2.5-inch SSD needs an adapter bracket to fit a 3.5-inch bay.
5.25 inches is the size of a desktop optical drive bay, too large for a laptop.
8 inches was the size of the first floppy disks, not a laptop drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.1 question 11
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.1 (laptop hardware)

stem: You are having trouble with your voice recognition technology on your Windows 10 laptop. Which of the following tasks should you perform FIRST to resolve this issue with minimal effort?
options: Get an up-to-date driver for the voice recognition software
Enable apps to access your microphone
explanation: In Windows, if the microphone is not working properly, go to Privacy, select Microphone, and ensure the Allow apps to access your microphone feature is turned on. This is a quick setting change, so it is the first thing to check.
whyWrong: Rebooting the laptop is unlikely to resolve the issue if apps are blocked from the microphone.
An up-to-date driver will not help if apps have not been allowed to access the microphone.
An external microphone would be blocked by the same privacy setting and costs more effort.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.2 question 6
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.2 (mobile display components); the laptop microphone is current 1.1. The Windows privacy setting also relates to 220-1202/1.6 (Privacy).

stem: A computer technician is troubleshooting wireless connectivity on a laptop. Where do you think is the MOST LIKELY location for the wireless antenna?
options: On the front of the laptop
On the rear of the laptop
On the top of the laptop
Near the fan on the base of the laptop
explanation: The wireless antenna is normally located in the bezel at the top of the laptop's display. Placing it high in the lid gives it the best reception.
whyWrong: The front of a laptop has no antenna; it is blocked by the user and the chassis.
The rear of the base is near the hinge and metal parts, so antennas are not placed there.
An antenna in the base near the fan would be shielded by metal parts and get a poor signal.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.2 question 14
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.2 (mobile display components); Wi-Fi antenna placement is current 1.1.

stem: Where is the built-in camera/webcam module of a laptop usually located?
options: Under the keyboard, next to the RAM
Above the display screen, behind the display bezel
explanation: A laptop's camera/webcam module sits above the display screen, behind the display bezel. To replace it, the technician removes the bezel, then disconnects the module's small plug with a non-metal prying tool.
whyWrong: RAM may sit under the keyboard, but the webcam must face the user from the display.
The battery compartment holds the battery, not a camera that must see the user.
The touchpad area holds the pointing device and its cables, not the camera.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

stem: A user reports that the built-in webcam on a laptop shows no picture in any app. What should the technician do FIRST?
options: Replace the webcam module with an identical part
Check whether the camera is turned off with a function key or in the operating system
explanation: Many laptops can turn off the camera with a function key, and the operating system can disable it too. Check these settings before you open the display to replace the webcam module.
whyWrong: Replacing the module comes only after the function key and operating system settings are checked.
The display assembly is a costly part to replace, and nothing points to the display itself.
Reinstalling the operating system is a last resort, not a first step for a disabled camera.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

stem: A company's security policy says the laptops must not be able to record sound or video in a secure area. A user has put tape over the webcam lens and the microphone openings. What is the BEST way to meet the policy?
options: Add a second layer of tape
Disable or remove the webcam module, which usually includes the microphone
explanation: Tape over the microphone openings can muffle the sound, but the microphone can still record. On most laptops the microphone is part of the webcam module above the display, so disabling or removing that module stops both video and sound.
whyWrong: More tape still only muffles the sound, so the microphone can record.
The speaker volume controls playback, not what the microphone records.
Turning off Wi-Fi stops the network connection, but the camera and microphone can still record locally.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

stem: In Windows, where can a technician disable a laptop's built-in microphone?
options: The Recording tab of the Sound dialog box
The Playback tab of the Sound dialog box
explanation: The Recording tab of the Sound dialog box lists the input devices, such as the built-in microphone, and lets you disable them. It is a quick way to turn off the microphone without removing hardware.
whyWrong: The Playback tab lists output devices such as speakers and headphones.
Disk Management manages drives and partitions, not audio devices.
Power Options sets sleep and power plans, not audio input devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

stem: A user unplugged an external keyboard and now types on the laptop's own keyboard. Some letter keys type numbers instead of letters. What is the MOST LIKELY cause?
options: Num Lock is on, so the keys with a second number function type numbers
The keyboard was disabled in Device Manager
explanation: On a small laptop keyboard, some letter keys share a numeric keypad function that Num Lock turns on. This often happens after the user disconnects an external keyboard, and pressing Num Lock once fixes it.
whyWrong: A loose ribbon cable makes keys fail completely, not type numbers.
A failed driver would stop the keyboard working, not change letters into numbers.
A disabled keyboard would not type anything at all.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

stem: A technician has replaced a laptop's keyboard and put the laptop back together. What should the technician do NEXT?
options: Test every key, including the Fn-enabled keys, in a text editor
Close the ticket without a test
explanation: After a keyboard replacement, verify the repair: test every key in Notepad or another text editor, and test the Fn-enabled keys too. Only then is the repair complete.
whyWrong: Nothing points to the touchpad, so replacing it adds cost without a reason.
A firmware update is not part of a keyboard replacement.
The repair must be verified before the ticket is closed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

stem: Which type of charging connector would you find on an iPad? (Select all that apply.)
explanation: The Lightning connector is one of Apple’s proprietary charging and synchronization connectors used by older iPads and iPhones. Today, Apple uses USB-C.
whyWrong: microUSB is used by older Android-based mobile devices, not iPads.
IP68 is an ingress protection rating against dust and water, not a connector.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which of the following can be useful in areas where a smartphone has cellular access but a PC (or laptop) cannot connect to the Internet?
explanation: Tethering and hotspotting can allow a desktop computer or laptop to share the mobile device’s Internet connection. Tethering and hotspotting functionality can be very useful in areas where a smartphone has cellular access but a PC/laptop cannot connect to the Internet.
whyWrong: A proprietary vendor-specific connector is a charging or sync port and does not share an Internet connection by itself.
Accessories such as headsets, speakers, and battery packs are useful but do not connect a PC to the Internet.
IP codes such as IP68 rate a device’s protection against dust and water.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: A user has asked you to provide a more accurate way of manipulating their smartphone screen. This user is part of a mobile salesforce and needs to be able to work quickly and efficiently. Which of the following is the easiest and BEST solution?
options: Connect an external monitor so that the images on the screen will be bigger.
Configure a drawing pad to work with the smartphone.
Set up a touch pen to access the screen directly.
Add an external touchpad to the device.
explanation: The best option is to set up a touch pen to access the smartphone’s screen directly. A smartphone may come with a touch pen (also known as a stylus pen or simply a stylus); or it may be able to have a touch pen added later. A touch pen enables a person to input information to the screen more accurately.
whyWrong: An external monitor makes the user much less mobile and does not make input more accurate.
A drawing pad is extra hardware that makes mobility more difficult for a traveling salesforce.
An external touchpad would work, but it is extra hardware to carry and not the easiest solution.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which of the following refers to a small, pressure-sensitive nub typically found on Lenovo ThinkPad keyboards, which acts as a pointing device allowing users to control the cursor on the screen without lifting their hands from the keyboard?
explanation: A track point refers to a small, pressure-sensitive nub typically found on Lenovo ThinkPad keyboards, which acts as a pointing device allowing users to control the cursor on the screen without lifting their hands from the keyboard. It works like a mini joystick between the G, H, and B keys.
whyWrong: A trackpad is a flat surface on a laptop where users slide their fingers to move the cursor.
A touchpad is another name for the flat trackpad surface below a laptop keyboard, not a nub between the keys.
Mini joystick describes how a track point behaves, but it is not the name of the device.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: One of your coworkers has asked for a cable for an Apple iPhone 16 that can charge it and transfer data to and from it. Which of the following connection types would meet your coworker’s requirements?
explanation: USB-C is a universally accepted standard that enables charging, syncing data, and playing audio and video. From the iPhone 15 on, Apple switched over to USB-C.
whyWrong: Apple devices do not use Micro-USB, which is common on Android-based devices.
Lightning is the proprietary Apple connector that the iPhone 14 was the last iPhone to use.
Apple devices do not use Mini-USB, although adapters may be available.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 17

stem: Which of the following mobile phone technologies is responsible for contactless pay like Apple Pay?
explanation: Near-field communication (NFC) is the short-ranged technology that contactless payment systems like Apple Pay and Google Wallet use. Because NFC works only over a few centimeters, the phone must be held close to the payment terminal.
whyWrong: IMSI is the International Mobile Subscriber Identity, which identifies the user of a cellular network.
RFID uses tags and radio-frequency scanning to identify those tags, not to make phone payments.
Bluetooth is mainly used to connect peripherals, such as a headset to a smartphone.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 36

stem: A user needs to get their laptop connected to the Internet, but no Wi-Fi connections are available. They do have their smartphone with them. What is the BEST option for them to get Internet access for their laptop?
explanation: Tethering is connecting a device to an Internet hotspot. One assumes in this case that the smartphone can function as a hotspot, and then the laptop will tether to it either via Wi-Fi or a wired connection. The smartphone shares its cellular data connection with the laptop.
whyWrong: NFC is a very short-range technology for tasks such as contactless payments and quick pairing, not for sharing an Internet connection.
Lightning is Apple's wired connector for charging and data, not a way to provide Internet access by itself.
Bluetooth is meant for short-range accessories and file exchange, and the book does not count it as a way to share the Internet connection here.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 5

stem: You need to wirelessly connect two accessories to a smartphone. Which of the following could be valid options to connect these wireless accessories? (Choose two.)
explanation: Two wireless connectivity options are NFC and Bluetooth; hotspot (not mentioned) is the third. USB and Lightning are wired connectivity methods.
whyWrong: USB is a wired connection method.
Lightning is Apple's wired connector, not a wireless option.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 8

stem: You have a user who needs to keep desktop devices such as keyboard, monitor, and mouse permanently connected so that they can be used by an attached laptop. What type of device do you recommend that they use?
explanation: A docking station made specifically for its associated brand and model of laptop can host desktop components permanently, regardless of whether the laptop is attached to the docking station. When the laptop's portability is not required, but instead use of the desktop components is the priority, attaching the laptop to the docking station makes such components available to the laptop without separately attaching each component.
whyWrong: A KVM switch shares one keyboard, monitor, and mouse among several computers, not a permanent desk setup for one laptop.
There is no input/output virtual server accessory for laptops.
A USB hub adds USB ports but does not provide video and the other connections of a docking station.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 14

stem: One of your network users has an older laptop with no Bluetooth support. He recently received a Bluetooth headset that he needs to use with his laptop. What is the quickest and cheapest way to make the headset compatible with his laptop?
options: Buy a Mini PCIe Bluetooth adapter.
explanation: A USB Bluetooth adapter should do the trick. There are Mini PCIe Bluetooth adapters, but installing one is trickier than inserting a USB device. Replacing the laptop is a much more expensive proposition.
whyWrong: There aren't really any Wi-Fi compatible headsets on the market, because headsets are what Bluetooth was designed for.
A Mini PCIe Bluetooth adapter works but must be installed inside the laptop, which is slower and harder than plugging in USB.
Replacing the laptop is far more expensive than adding an adapter.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 19

stem: A user wants her laptop to have a full-sized optical drive and external hard drive. Which of the following accessories is MOST LIKELY to have full-sized bays for these devices?
explanation: A docking station is a device that a laptop can be plugged into that replicates common laptop ports, and may also have full-sized bays for PC desktop expansion cards and storage devices, such as hard drives and optical drives. A port replicator will replicate laptop ports but does not usually have expansion bays.
whyWrong: There is no specific laptop base accessory with drive bays.
A port replicator copies the laptop's ports but does not usually have expansion bays.
There is no Mini PCIe dock; Mini PCIe is an internal laptop technology.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 20

stem: Which of the following connectors is unique to Apple devices?
explanation: Lightning connectors are an Apple proprietary connector type developed to be used with Apple's mobile devices. Newer iPhones and iPads have moved to USB-C, but Lightning remains Apple-only.
whyWrong: USB-C is an industry standard used by many manufacturers, including Apple.
Molex is a power connector for internal desktop drives, not an Apple connector.
USB-A is the common rectangular USB connector used across all platforms.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 24: Mobile Devices, Chapter Review question 6
note: All-in-One 11e Chapter 24 (old 220-1101 1.3); matches current 1.2 connection methods.

stem: Leonard just purchased a very expensive comic book and paid for it using the stored credit card information on his smartphone. What technology did he use to make the transaction?
explanation: Leonard likely purchased his comic book using Near Field Communication (NFC) technology, which can be used for payment transactions through stored credit card information in mobile applications. NFC works only over a few centimeters, so the phone is held next to the payment terminal.
whyWrong: Swipe lock is a screen lock method, not a payment technology.
Wi-Fi calling routes phone calls over a Wi-Fi network and has nothing to do with payments.
BitLocker To Go encrypts removable drives in Windows.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 24: Mobile Devices, Chapter Review question 8
note: All-in-One 11e Chapter 24 (old 220-1101 1.3); matches current 1.2 NFC.

stem: A client wants to connect an external keyboard to an Android tablet. Which of the following connection types are appropriate for this task? ( Choose two)
explanation: The easiest of the available options is a Bluetooth-enabled keyboard paired with the Android tablet. Android tablets also have a USB-C port, so a USB-C keyboard or a USB-C adapter for a USB keyboard works too.
whyWrong: Tablets do not have Ethernet ports because they are too thin, and Ethernet does not connect keyboards.
Lightning connectors are used only by Apple phones and tablets, not Android tablets.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.1 question 13
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.1 (laptop hardware); connection methods are current 1.2. The book's explanation said the USB-C connector goes to DVI or HDMI, which does not apply to a keyboard; that sentence was replaced.

stem: What is the most common use of NFC?
explanation: Near-Field Communication (NFC) is most commonly used for contactless card and phone payments. It works only over a few centimeters, which suits tap-to-pay readers.
whyWrong: A hotspot is created by tethering, which shares the phone's cellular data over Wi-Fi, USB, or Bluetooth.
Touchscreen input comes from the digitizer, not from NFC.
A VPN is created by dedicated VPN software, not by NFC.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.1 question 14
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.1 (laptop hardware); NFC is a connection method in current 1.2.

stem: The external webcam attached to a laptop is switched on, but it is not producing any images. Which of the following can resolve this issue?
options: Reboot the computer and try again
Uninstall and then reinstall the webcam software and ensure you have the most up-to-date drivers from the manufacturer’s website
Plug the webcam into another USB port
explanation: Since the webcam is switched on but shows no image, it is likely to be a software or driver setup issue. Reinstalling the webcam software with the latest drivers from the manufacturer's website is the best solution.
whyWrong: Rebooting the computer will not resolve a webcam software or driver issue.
Purchasing a new webcam is unnecessary when the camera powers on and the fault is in its software.
The webcam is already switched on, so the USB port is supplying it and moving it is unlikely to fix the image.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.2 question 3
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.2 (mobile display components); an external webcam is an accessory in current 1.2.

stem: The touchpad on your laptop is unresponsive. What should you do? ( Choose two)
options: Remove an external mouse that is plugged in
explanation: The touchpad (also called the trackpad) can be used instead of a mouse, and some laptops disable it when an external mouse is plugged in. If it is unresponsive, first remove any external mouse; if that does not work, update the touchpad driver.
whyWrong: Rebooting the laptop will not re-enable a touchpad that is disabled by a mouse or a bad driver.
A gyroscope rotates the screen on phones and tablets and has nothing to do with the touchpad.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.2 question 16
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.2 (mobile display components); the trackpad is current 1.2.

stem: What type of connection does an iPhone 10 charger use?
explanation: The charger for the iPhone X (iPhone 10) uses a Lightning cable. Apple used the Lightning connector from the iPhone 5 until the iPhone 15 moved to USB-C.
whyWrong: USB-B is the square connector used by printers.
USB-A is the flat host connector on computers, TVs, and gaming consoles.
USB-C is used by Android phones and most other new devices, but not by the iPhone X.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 1
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3 (mobile accessories and ports); connection methods are current 1.2.

stem: A user is trying to plug a USB 3.0 memory stick into their old Windows 7 laptop but is having difficulty doing so. Which of the following could be causing the issue? ( Choose two)
options: The USB 3.0 drive has a different form factor
The USB 3.0 drive is upside down
The laptop does not have a USB 3.0 port
The end of the USB 3.0 drive is damaged
explanation: If the drive does not physically fit, the most likely causes are a connector of a different form factor (for example a USB-C drive and a USB-A port) or a damaged or bent connector. USB 3.0 Type-A drives are backward compatible with USB 2.0 Type-A ports, so the port version does not stop the drive from plugging in.
whyWrong: Users try a USB drive both ways around, so being upside down is quickly ruled out.
A USB 3.0 Type-A drive fits a USB 2.0 Type-A port and simply runs at USB 2.0 speed.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 2
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3 (mobile accessories and ports). Book answer A and C corrected to A and D: USB 3.0 Type-A is backward compatible with USB 2.0 ports, so a missing USB 3.0 port does not make the drive hard to insert; a damaged connector does.

stem: What type of connection does a Samsung Galaxy phone use?
explanation: Current Samsung Galaxy phones use a USB-C connector. Older Galaxy models used micro-USB, but USB-C replaced it from the Galaxy S8 onward.
whyWrong: No phone uses a full-size USB Type-A connector as its port.
Micro-USB was used by older Galaxy phones and is now found on small devices such as power banks and controllers.
Mini-USB was used by early smartphones, PDAs, and cameras.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 3
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3 (mobile accessories and ports)

stem: Which of the following types of functionality would a docking station with DisplayPort provide for a laptop user? ( Choose four)
explanation: A docking station is a sophisticated port replicator. Docking stations usually provide USB ports for a keyboard and mouse, audio jacks for speakers, an RJ45 Ethernet port, and with DisplayPort, dual-monitor support.
whyWrong: Wi-Fi comes from the laptop's own wireless card, not from a docking station.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 6
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3 (mobile accessories and ports). Book answer A, D, E (Choose three) corrected to A, C, D, E (Choose four): docking stations normally include a wired Ethernet port.

stem: A user is working remotely from home and is due to participate in a Zoom conference call in 15 minutes. Unfortunately, when they boot up their laptop, they find their home wireless network is down. What can the user implement quickly so that they can participate in the conference call? Choose the solution that requires the minimum amount of effort.
options: Travel 10 miles to the local Starbucks to use their wireless network
Connect the laptop directly to the wireless router using an Ethernet cable
Create a hotspot using a smartphone
explanation: Using a smartphone to create a personal hotspot is the fastest way to get internet access on the laptop. The phone shares its cellular data connection over Wi-Fi, so the call can start within minutes.
whyWrong: Traveling 10 miles might make the user miss the call, and the conversation could be overheard in a public place.
An Ethernet cable to a router that has no internet connection still gives no internet access.
Rebooting the router will not restore the internet when the home network is down.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 7
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3 (mobile accessories and ports); hotspot is in current 1.2 (tethering/hotspot) and 1.3 (enable hotspot).

stem: A laptop user has been complaining to the help desk that their laptop does not have that many ports. They would like a range of additional ports for a keyboard, a mouse, and a VGA projector. How can the support desk fulfill this request with the least amount of administrative work?
explanation: A port replicator plugs into a laptop to give the user a range of additional ports, such as USB for a keyboard and mouse and VGA for a projector. It is a quick hardware install with no configuration.
whyWrong: A KVM switch shares one keyboard, video display, and mouse between several computers; it does not add ports to a laptop.
Dual monitors only add a second screen and do not give ports for a keyboard, mouse, and projector.
A USB hub adds only USB ports, so it cannot connect a VGA projector.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 8
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3 (mobile accessories and ports)

stem: What type of connection was micro USB replaced by?
explanation: The micro-USB connection was replaced by USB-C on most phones and small devices. USB-C is reversible and supports faster data and charging.
whyWrong: Serial cables are legacy RS-232 cables, not a replacement for micro-USB.
Lightning connectors are used only by Apple devices and did not replace micro-USB.
Parallel cables are old printer cables that were replaced by USB.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 10
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3 (mobile accessories and ports)

stem: What type of connection does an iPhone 14 charger use?
explanation: The iPhone 14 uses a Lightning connector for charging. Apple moved the iPhone to USB-C with the iPhone 15 in 2023.
whyWrong: USB-A is the flat host connector on computers, TVs, and gaming consoles.
USB-B is the square connector used by printers.
USB-C replaced Lightning starting with the iPhone 15, not the iPhone 14.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 11
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3 (mobile accessories and ports). Book answer C (USB-C) corrected to D (Lightning): the iPhone 14 has a Lightning port; USB-C came with the iPhone 15.

stem: A user is trying to connect to a Zoom session, but when they select the video option, it fails to open. They then go to the camera app on their desktop to test the webcam, but the webcam also fails to open. The webcam was working the previous day. Which of the following should be done to address this issue? ( Choose two)
options: Ensure that in the camera privacy settings, Allow apps to access this camera is enabled
Unplug the webcam USB cable and try another USB port
Close any other video software applications and turn on the webcam to see whether it will launch
Purchase another webcam as the webcam is broken
explanation: Web cameras can only provide input to one application at a time, so close any other video software first. If the privacy setting Allow apps to access this camera is not enabled, the webcam will not work in any app.
whyWrong: The webcam worked yesterday, so moving it to another USB port is unlikely to fix the issue.
A new webcam would not fix a software clash or a blocked camera privacy setting.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 13
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3 (mobile accessories and ports); the webcam is a current 1.2 accessory; the privacy setting also relates to 220-1202/1.6.

stem: Following an update to the operating system of their desktop computer, the user’s webcam is no longer functioning. The user is due to join a Zoom session in 45 minutes time. Which of the following should be their FIRST step to resolve the issue?
options: Quickly go to the shops and buy another webcam
Reinstall the webcam software including any driver updates
explanation: When a webcam stops working after an operating system update, the driver is the likely cause. Uninstall it and reinstall the webcam software with the latest drivers from the manufacturer's website.
whyWrong: The webcam is most likely fine, and there may not be enough time to buy and set up a new one before the meeting.
The update has most likely already rebooted the computer, so another reboot is unlikely to help.
The operating system was just updated, and that update is the cause of the issue.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 15
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3 (mobile accessories and ports); the webcam is a current 1.2 accessory.

stem: A Cornish pasty vendor in Waterloo railway station is having difficulty taking contactless card payments. When the card is tapped, the contactless scanner does not read the card and process the transaction. The customers need to insert their card into the device and enter their pin to make payments. Which of the following technologies is at fault here?
explanation: Contactless card payments use NFC, where the card must be within about four inches of the reader. If tapping fails but inserting the card works, the NFC reader is at fault.
whyWrong: Contactless cards do not use Bluetooth, which is a pairing-based connection for accessories.
Contactless cards do not connect over Wi-Fi wireless networks.
Infrared needs a line of sight and is not used by contactless payment cards.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 16
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3 (mobile accessories and ports)

stem: Which of the following cable types did the Lightning cable replace?
explanation: Apple introduced the reversible Lightning connector in 2012 to replace the Apple 30-pin dock connector. Lightning was itself replaced by USB-C from the iPhone 15.
whyWrong: Apple never used a 20-pin phone connector.
Apple never used a 25-pin phone connector.
USB-C replaced Lightning, not the other way around.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 18
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3 (mobile accessories and ports)

stem: Which of the following connections require a username, password, and SMTP server? (Select the two best answers.)
explanation: POP3 and IMAP email connections require an incoming mail server (either POP3 or IMAP) and an outgoing mail server (SMTP). The user also signs in to these servers with a username and password.
whyWrong: A Bluetooth connection needs no username or SMTP server, though it might require a PIN.
A Wi-Fi connection usually needs a passcode but no username or SMTP server.
Exchange connections need a username and password but no SMTP server, because Exchange Server acts as both the incoming and outgoing mail server.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: When manually configuring a Wi-Fi connection, which step occurs after successfully entering the SSID?
options: Check whether the device is within range of the WAP.
Enter a passcode for the network.
explanation: After you enter the correct SSID, you enter the passcode (or passphrase) for the network. Scanning for networks comes first, so by the time the SSID is entered only the passcode remains before you connect.
whyWrong: POP3 has to do with configuring an email account, not a Wi-Fi connection.
If you have already entered the SSID, you should already be within range of the wireless access point.
Scanning for networks is the first step of a Wi-Fi setup, which happens before the SSID is entered.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which of the following allows other mobile devices to wirelessly share a mobile device’s Internet connection?
explanation: Mobile hotspot technology (sometimes referred to as Wi-Fi tethering) allows a mobile device to share its Internet connection with other Wi-Fi-capable devices. Another possibility would be USB tethering, but that is done in a wired fashion.
whyWrong: NFC lets two mobile devices send information to each other when they are in close proximity.
Airplane mode disables all wireless connectivity, including cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth.
IMAP is an email protocol similar to POP3.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Which of the following identifies the user of a device?
explanation: International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI) or an IMSI ID is used to identify the user of a device. For GSM, UMTS, and LTE networks, this ID is loaded into the SIM card or eSIM.
whyWrong: The IMEI (International Mobile Equipment Identity) identifies the device itself, not its user.
S/MIME is used to encrypt and sign email for authentication and message integrity.
A VPN makes secure connections by tunneling through the provider’s network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which of the following is used to synchronize contacts from an iPad to a PC? (Select the best answer.)
explanation: PC users need iTunes to synchronize contacts and other data from an iPad to a PC. You can also use the new Apple Devices app to do this as well.
whyWrong: Gmail can synchronize contacts, but it is based entirely on web storage and nothing is stored on the iPad.
Google Play is a place to get applications and other items for Android.
Sync Center is a Control Panel utility that enables synchronization across Windows devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: You oversee a midsized enterprise and are supporting 300 smartphones. Which of the following would BEST allow you to configure them from a centralized location?
explanation: Mobile device management (MDM) allows a person to centrally administer many mobile devices from a single workstation. From the MDM console, an administrator can push configurations, enforce policies, and deploy corporate apps to every phone.
whyWrong: GPS is a satellite-based navigation system that helps a device find its location.
Location services is a generic term for the services that locate a mobile device and provide mapping information to apps.
SSL/TLS is a protocol that encrypts data sent between devices on the Internet.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: What should you do after you have found a Bluetooth device for pairing? (Select two.)
explanation: CompTIA lists the Bluetooth connection process in the following order: Enable Bluetooth, enable pairing, find a device for pairing, enter the appropriate PIN code, and finally, test connectivity. So after the device is found, the two remaining steps are entering the PIN code and testing connectivity.
whyWrong: Enabling Bluetooth is the first step and must happen before you can find a device.
Pairing must be enabled, not disabled, for the devices to connect.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support, Cram Quiz question 7

stem: What is the secure port for POP3 email connections that make use of SSL/TLS?
explanation: The secure port for POP3 email connections that make use of SSL/TLS is 995. Port 110 is the default port for unencrypted POP3.
whyWrong: Port 110 is the POP3 default non-encrypted port.
Ports 465 and 587 are the secure port numbers for SMTP.
Port 993 is the secure port number for IMAP.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support, Cram Quiz question 8

stem: Which is a policy that governs employees bringing personally owned devices (laptops, smartphones, and the like) to the workplace and the use of those devices to access company data?
explanation: Bring your own device (BYOD) is a policy governing employees bringing personally owned devices (laptops, smartphones, and the like) to the workplace and the use of those devices to access company data. The BYOD, CYOD, or COPE policies should address how data and corporate-owned applications will be handled when employees are hired, terminated, quit, or retire.
whyWrong: CYOD lets employees select their devices from a limited list of company-approved options.
With COPE, the business owns and pays for the devices, which employees may also use personally.
ITU IMT-2020 is the 5G cellular standard, not a device ownership policy.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support, Cram Quiz question 9

stem: What should you do after you have located a device for pairing during the Bluetooth connection process?
options: Turn both devices off and then back on.
explanation: CompTIA lists the Bluetooth connection process in the following order: Enable Bluetooth, enable pairing, find a device for pairing, enter the appropriate PIN code, and, finally, test connectivity. So once a device is located, the next step is to enter its PIN code.
whyWrong: Testing connectivity is the final step and comes after you enter the PIN code.
You don’t have to turn the devices off and back on during the connection process.
Enabling Bluetooth is the first step, which is done before you locate a device.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 9

stem: When a mobile device is put into airplane mode, which of the following features are typically disabled? (Select the two best answers.)
explanation: Cellular connections are disabled when a mobile device enters airplane mode, and so are other wireless connections, such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, GPS, and NFC. However, on some devices, some of these other wireless technologies can be turned on individually after the device has been placed in airplane mode.
whyWrong: The display’s multitouch capability keeps working as normal in airplane mode.
Data encryption still functions, though the encrypted data cannot be sent anywhere.
The camera still works, but posting images and video to a remote source will not.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 16

stem: A friend asks you why she would ever disable cellular data networking. Which of the following is not a valid reason to disable cellular data networking?
options: You have a limited amount of data in your monthly plan.
You have access to a reliable Wi-Fi signal.
You are about to download an update to your phone.
Your phone calls are going out over your carrier's cellular network.
explanation: Whenever you have a reliable Wi-Fi signal available, which you do not pay for “as you go,” you should feel free to disable your cellular access to data networking. The wireless network is often faster and does not cost you anything to use. You can also disable cellular data for large downloads, such as updates, so they do not use your data plan. Phone calls will continue to be sent over the cellular network, so they are not a reason to disable cellular data.
whyWrong: A limited monthly data plan is a valid reason to turn off cellular data.
A reliable Wi-Fi signal is often faster and free, so it is a valid reason to turn off cellular data.
Turning off cellular data before a large download such as an update keeps it from using the data plan.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support, Review Questions question 1

stem: You need to pair two Bluetooth devices with each other. Which of the following is true regarding Bluetooth pairing?
options: Bluetooth connections support wireless device control but not file transfers.
Bluetooth is not yet a fully standardized protocol.
Bluetooth connections do not reach as far as Wi-Fi connections.
You must reboot the paired devices to complete the connection.
explanation: The range of Bluetooth connections is considered short compared to Wi-Fi connections. Bluetooth is a fully standardized protocol that supports file transfers. Rebooting, or even restarting, paired devices is not a requirement for Bluetooth connection.
whyWrong: Bluetooth supports file transfers as well as device control.
Bluetooth is a fully standardized protocol (IEEE 802.15).
Paired devices do not need a reboot to complete a Bluetooth connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support, Review Questions question 2

stem: A technician is configuring a mobile client to use email through an ISP. Which port number should he configure to use SMTP?
explanation: SMTP sends mail to the server on TCP port 25. POP3 uses port 110, and IMAP4 uses port 143. POP3 uses port 995 securely over SSL or TLS.
whyWrong: Port 110 is used by POP3 to download mail.
Port 143 is used by IMAP4 to access mail.
Port 995 is used by POP3 over SSL or TLS.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support, Review Questions question 3
note: Mail port configuration on a mobile device (1.3 business apps: mail); the ports themselves are also 220-1201/2.1.

stem: You need to configure email for a mobile client. His device has a setting referring to port 587. Which mail protocol is likely using this protocol?
explanation: SMTP with TLS uses port 587 by default. With SSL, SMTP uses port 465. IMAP4 with SSL/TLS uses port 993, whereas POP3 with SSL/TLS uses port 995.
whyWrong: SMTP with SSL uses port 465.
IMAP4 with SSL/TLS uses port 993.
POP3 with SSL/TLS uses port 995.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support, Review Questions question 4
